minutes.headline: Conservation Commission approved the Lake Shirley boat ramp rebuild with wetland buffer waivers.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Conservation Commission held a long session covering multiple RDAs, NOIs, tree-removal determinations and a certificate of compliance, approving several routine wetland-adjacent projects (a cemetery expansion, septic repairs, a shed/sand permit, tree removals) with standard conditions. The major substantive action was approval of the Shady Point boat ramp reconstruction on Lake Shirley with buffer-zone waivers after public debate over impervious-surface classification and a retaining wall versus riprap; several other hearings (404 Page Street, 108 Sunny Hill Road, the Violet irrigation pond, 141 Pleasant Street) were continued to October 7. The commission also discussed Hollis Road residence budget items, a storm water utility warrant article, and a resolved no-trespass situation at the Pleasant Street Conservation Area.

what_happened.line: The commission approved the Lake Shirley boat ramp rebuild at Shady Point, granting waivers to work inside the normal 30-foot no-disturb and 50-foot no-build wetland buffers.
Four other wetland hearings, including a new house and driveway at 404 Page Street, were continued to October 7 rather than decided.
The commission approved three routine RDAs with standard conditions: a DPW cemetery expansion, a septic force main repair, and a shed/sand permit.
A non-binding warrant article was finalized asking whether storm water funding should move out of the operating budget into a dedicated storm water utility.
A vote on replacing flooring at the town-owned Hollis Road residence was deferred pending clarification of a vendor's deposit request.

why_it_matters: The boat ramp decision sets a precedent for allowing construction inside protected wetland buffers along Lake Shirley when a project shows a public benefit.

The storm water warrant article, if it reaches town meeting, would ask voters to decide whether storm water work gets its own dedicated funding stream instead of competing inside the general operating budget.
Residents near 404 Page Street, 108 Sunny Hill Road, the Violet irrigation pond, and 141 Pleasant Street will have another chance to be heard before any of those projects are decided.
watch_next: October 7, 2026: continued hearings for 404 Page Street, 108 Sunny Hill Road, the Violet irrigation pond, and 141 Pleasant Street
The storm water utility warrant article, as submitted for an upcoming town meeting

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on every substantive vote they share: the three RDAs, the boat ramp order, the three tree removals, the certificate of compliance, the mosquito-control work and the 108 Sunny Hill Road continuance. Most differences are caption misspellings of names. The main gap is that our minutes record continuance votes for four hearings (141 Pleasant Street, 404 Page Street, the Cry Nature Center and the Unitil substation) plus the Violet pond, and the official minutes record none of them.
